summary: Right-handed baseball pitcher at stride-foot contact: long stride landing slightly closed, hips opening while the shoulders stay closed, throwing arm up in the 90/90 position, glove arm pointing at the plate.

environment.name: plate
environment.text: Pitching from a mound 25 cm high; home plate 18.44 m ahead along the direction of play (the floor here is drawn flat).

cameras.name: catcher_view
cameras.text: Broadcast view from behind the plate, long telephoto compression, sharp focus on the pitcher.

cameras.name: first_base_side
cameras.text: Side view from the first-base side: stride and arm path read clearly.

cameras.name: low_cinema
cameras.text: Low wide cinematic frame from the grass in front of the mound, stadium lights behind.

rules.why: stride about 83 % of height (ankle to ankle 150 +/- 15 cm); the model allows 1.5 SD below the mean
external rotation about 30-56 deg at foot contact
hips open ahead of the closed shoulders (separation about 30 deg)

text.action: a right-handed baseball pitcher landing the stride foot with the throwing arm cocked in the 90/90 position
text.core: Long stride about 83 % of body height, left foot planted slightly closed toward the third-base side of the line, left knee bent about 50 degrees; right pivot foot still on the rubber on its toes; hips opening toward the plate while the shoulders stay closed; right upper arm level with the shoulders and behind the shoulder line, elbow bent 90 degrees, forearm raised and pointing up, ball facing away from the plate; glove arm extended toward home plate.
text.gaze: Eyes locked on the catcher's mitt.
cues: stride about 80-85 % of height, landing slightly closed
throwing arm up in the 90/90 position
hips open while the shoulders stay closed
glove arm points at the target
kinetic: dirt spraying from the landing foot
jersey stretched across the chest by the hip-shoulder separation
motion blur on the stride leg, face sharp

sources.cite: Driveline OpenBiomechanics, baseball_pitching (100 pitchers, 411 fastballs, 1.85 +/- 0.07 m): means computed from the dataset's point-of-interest and full-signal files (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; only summary numbers used here)
Fleisig, ISBS 2010 keynote: stride 83 +/- 4 % of height, lead knee 45 deg, shoulder abduction 93 deg, ER 56 deg, elbow 90 deg at foot contact
A Clinician's Guide to Analysis of the Pitching Motion (2019): balance point, 90/90 arm position, MER about 170 deg
Biomechanical Analysis of the Throwing Athlete, Arthrosc Sports Med Rehabil 2022: stride over 80 % of height, MER 170-180 deg
